answer: Each agent keeps its own atlas: an append-only map of every job it finished, with the raw outputs. Validators spot-check it via random proofs of storage, asking for byte ranges no other agent could hold. Clones can't share one copy, since each atlas is unique, so a fake fleet must store and serve terabytes per identity. That basalt-heavy cost, paid daily, makes a Sybil harbor too expensive to keep.
